description:
Apply the frozen adoption rules to the private BitSlice prototype and decide whether an integration through existing private abstractions is justified.

## Background

BitSlice remains a bit view and no new public borrowed-word API is authorized by this story. A qualifying consumer gain may justify a private integration design. If realizing it requires a lasting public API or shared-infrastructure change, this branch closes as no-adoption, records the pending owner decision for a later explicitly authorized container, and does not block story completion.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The decision applies the predeclared worthwhile-effect, equivalence-margin, complexity, and whole-consumer rules to the private prototype evidence.
- [hard] REQ-02: A qualifying existing-abstraction result names one bounded private integration target, while a non-qualifying result preserves the no-win and leaves production unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: Evidence requiring a public borrowed-word API or shared infrastructure resolves here to no-adoption plus a pending owner decision for later work, without waiting for that decision.

## Notes

This issue selects whether private design work is warranted; it does not design or implement the integration.
title: Select the zero-copy integration outcome
